steps.message:
The build succeeds and the fix is verified in the compiled resources. Here's the diagnosis and patch.

## Root cause

The Robotic Arm servo controllers use a `SeekArc` whose progress range was the library default **0–100**, while the UI works in **0–360 degrees**. The activity therefore converted back and forth with a lossy scale factor of `3.6`, and papered over the resulting mismatch with an `editEnter` boolean flag:

```java
// onProgressChanged
if (editEnter) { degreeText1.setText(String.valueOf(degree)); editEnter = false; }
else           { degreeText1.setText(String.valueOf((int) (i * 3.6))); }

// processDegreeInput
seekArc.setProgress((int) (degree / 3.6));   // fires the listener synchronously!
editEnter = true;                            // set too late
```

`SeekArc.setProgress()` notifies the listener **synchronously**, so when the user typed `38`, the listener ran while `editEnter` was still `false` and overwrote the text with the round-tripped value `(int)(38/3.6) * 3.6 = (int)(10 * 3.6) = 36`. (The flag was then left dangling `true`, so the next drag would display a stale value too — a second symptom of the same hack.)

## Fix

1. **`servo_controller_layout.xml`** — give the arc the same resolution as the value range, so progress *is* the degree value and no rounding can occur:
   ```xml
   app:max="360"
   ```
   (verified in the built APK: `res-auto:max(0x7f0403ae)=360`)

2. **`RoboticArmActivity.java`** — removed the `3.6` conversions and the `editEnter`/shared-`degree` flag hack:
   - the four `onProgressChanged` callbacks simply display the progress value;
   - `processDegreeInput()` uses a local `degree`, calls `setProgress(degree)` directly, and re-asserts the text afterwards (necessary because `setProgress()` doesn't notify when the value is unchanged);
   - empty input now restores the arc's current value instead of relying on stale state;
   - `0`/`360` bounds are now the constants `MIN_DEGREE`/`MAX_DEGREE`, also reused by the `InputMinMaxFilter`s.

## Result for the reported steps
Drag to `100` → arc progress `100`, text `100`. Type `38`, press Enter → `setProgress(38)`, text `38`. The displayed value now always equals the entered value, and the thumb position matches it exactly (previously it could only land on multiples of 3.6°).

```java
editEnter = true;                            // set too late
```

`SeekArc.setProgress()` notifies the listener **synchronously**, so when the user typed `38`, the listener ran while `editEnter` was still `false` and overwrote the text with the round-tripped value `(int)(38/3.6) * 3.6 = (int)(10 * 3.6) = 36`. (The flag was then left dangling `true`, so the next drag would display a stale value too — a second symptom of the same hack.)

## Fix

1. **`servo_controller_layout.xml`** — give the arc the same resolution as the value range, so progress *is* the degree value and no rounding can occur:
   ```xml
   app:max="360"
   ```
   (verified in the built APK: `res-auto:max(0x7f0403ae)=360`)

2. **`RoboticArmActivity.java`** — removed the `3.6` conversions and the `editEnter`/shared-`degree` flag hack:
   - the four `onProgressChanged` callbacks simply display the progress value;
   - `processDegreeInput()` uses a local `degree`, calls `setProgress(degree)` directly, and re-asserts the text afterwards (necessary because `setProgress()` doesn't notify when the value is unchanged);
   - empty input now restores the arc's current value instead of relying on stale state;
   - `0`/`360` bounds are now the constants `MIN_DEGREE`/`MAX_DEGREE`, also reused by the `InputMinMaxFilter`s.

## Result for the reported steps
Drag to `100` → arc progress `100`, text `100`. Type `38`, press Enter → `setProgress(38)`, text `38`. The displayed value now always equals the entered value, and the thumb position matches it exactly (previously it could only land on multiples of 3.6°).
